angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 331,153 km at 182.00 pc = 0.02 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.4946 +/- 0.0652 mas (same row, RUWE 1.11): 182.00 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.476 +/- 0.013 solar radii from O'Brien et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-6158 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172..117O/abstract): 331,153 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.503 +/- 0.022 solar masses from O'Brien et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-6158 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172..117O/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3467 +/- 59 K from O'Brien et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-6158 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172..117O/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: O'Brien et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-6158 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172..117O/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-6158.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.784, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
